newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Council members still hopeful for Wed Iraq vote.
newsitem.headline: Council members still hopeful for Wed Iraq vote.

text.p: Russian ambassador Sergei Lavrov, this month's Security Council president, has tentatively scheduled a vote to renew the oil-for-food program for Iraq for Friday, but U.S. officials are shooting for adoption on Wednesday.
"I full expect that," one senior official told Reuters. A Protuguese council member said the vote was "likely on Wednesday" but there could be a day's delay.
U.S. officials said they wanted a brief document, being worked on privately by Security Council experts on Tuesday.

The current deal, which expires on June 7, calls for $2 billion worth of oil sales over six months so Baghdad can buy food and medicine for its people, suffering from sanctions imposed in August 1990 when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.

The U.S. officials said at this point they were concerned more about U.N. monitoring and implementation of the deal than the intricacies of the resolution. They said they had kept on hold all items destined for Iraq that were not emergency food and medicine because the U.N. did not have enough monitors on the ground yet for this purpose.
About two-thirds of the oil revenues are for humanitarian supplies, with the remainder earmarked for compensation of Gulf War victims and the costs of destroying Iraq's weapons of mass destruction.
